thread:
alex: morning handoff — quick summary from overnight. 02:34-03:10 we saw intermittent elevated routing latencies from router-prod-1 causing a spike in inference p95/p99 for a small subset of requests. Pager fired (oncall-bot) but auto-escalation stopped at primary. I left the short bridge notes below and the actions we took.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT #4821 triggered: routing-anomaly -> 502/504 spikes on region-us-west (detected 2026-04-10T02:34Z). Pager sent to alex primary, devon secondary.

maria: saw the same. traces showed requests hitting a single gateway pod that had eviction churn. suspect iptables restart from node maintenance.

chris: confirmed node k8s-gn-23 was drained around 02:20 for a kernel patch. some ephemeral connections didn't migrate cleanly, hit our sticky routing.

alex: mitigation performed: temporarily disabled strict-session-sticky on router pool for us-west and bumped retry budget. rolled back sticky change after confirming redistribution.

alex: commands run:
```
# remove sticky flag on router pool
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API' https://ops-api.internal/pools/us-west/router/policy -d '{"sticky":false}'
# bump retry budget
okctl patch routemap router-pool-us-west -p '{"retries":3}'
```

devon: i also increased burst_capacity for dedicated-pool-2 to avoid immediate 429s while the routers drained.

jordan: customer impact — minimal, ~7 customers saw latency spikes >2s for requests that went through the affected gateway. No error-rate increase for embeddings endpoints, mostly generation paths. Notified CS to watch for tickets.

maria: runbook links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/router-fallback and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/node-drain-checklist (both updated). next steps in runbook: verify KV-cache warm after pod reschedule and check autoscaler logs.

chris: open follow-ups — 1) investigate why drain caused sticky sessions to persist 2) add health-check backoff so we don't route to pods in mid-drain 3) add alert for sticky-session imbalance.

alex: handoff assignments for today: primary = maria, secondary = devon. i'm stepping off at 09:00 PT but reachable for escalation.

maria: taking primary. coverage note: i'm OOO tomorrow 14:00-18:00 PT — devon will be primary during that window.

devon: ack. i'll add a bookmark in the ops console with the commands run + link to the canary logs.

jordan: customer comms — CS notified; I'll draft a short note if we get any inbound tickets.

alex: outstanding: KV cache steady, no token-cost anomalies. latency p99 back to baseline by 03:18 after rollback and burst bump. documented timeline in the incident page: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4821

maria: next action items for primary shift: 1) run node-drain postmortem with infra team 2) add automation to flag nodes draining with active sticky sessions 3) follow up on autoscaler tuning ticket (ENG-805).

devon: i'll own ENG-805 and the autoscaler test. target EOD today for a draft.

alex: any blockers?

maria: none from me. everything stable. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: REMINDER: please update the oncall roster calendar and ACK this thread if you accepted handoff.

chris: acked and added notes to the incident page.

alex: okay — handing off, primary -> maria, secondary -> devon. please escalate to me if we see repeat routing anomalies.
